title: Celsus invents a claim no Christian made
source_text: Εἶτα πάλιν, ὡς ἔθος τῷ Κέλσῳ. φύρει ἐν τοῖς ἑξῆς λέγων ἃ οὐδεὶς ἡμῶν ἀνέγραψε· φησὶ γὰρ τοιαῦτα· οὐ μὴν οὐδὲ ἐκεῖνο ἀνεκτόν σου λέγοντος, ὡς, ἂν οἱ νῦν βασιλεύοντες ἡμῶν σοι πεισθέντες ἁλῶσι. τοὺς αὖθις βασιλεύοντας πείσεις εἶτ᾿ ἄλλους, ἂν κἀκεῖνοι ἁλῶσι, καὶ ἄλλους ἐπ᾿ ἄλλοις, μέχρι πάντων τῶν σοι πειθομένων ἁλισκομένων μία τις ἀρχὴ σωφρονήσασα καὶ προειδομένη τὸ συμβαῖνον πάντας ὑμᾶς, πρὶν αὐτὴν προαπολέσθαι, παγγενεὶ διολέσει. εἰπεῖν δὲ περὶ τούτων οὐχ αἱρεῖ λόγος, οὐ γὰρ λέγει τις ἡμῶν περὶ τῶν νῦν βασιλευόντων ὅτι, ἐὰν πεισθέντες ἁλῶσι, τοὺς μετ᾿ αὐτοὺς πάλιν πείσομεν, κἀκείνων ἁλόντων πάλιν τοὺς ἑξῆς πείσομεν. πόθεν δὲ καὶ ἀπέῤῥιψεν ὅτι κατὰ διαδοχὴν ἀεὶ τῶν ὑστέρων πειθομένων ἡμῖν καὶ ἁλισκομένων διὰ τὸ μὴ ἀμύνεσθαι τοὺς πολεμίους μία τις ἀρχὴ σωφρονήσασα καὶ προειδομένη τὸ συμβαῖνον παγγενεὶ ἡμᾶς διολέσει; ἀλλ᾿ ἔοικε φλυαρίας ἐν τούτοις ἑξῆς συνάπτων καὶ τοῦτ᾿ ἀφ᾿ ἑαυτοῦ ἀπεῤῥοιβδηκέναι.
pass_a_gloss: Then again, as custom (ἔθος) to Celsus, he mixes up (φύρω) in what follows, saying things which none of us wrote down (ἀναγράφω); for he says such things: [Celsus] 'not indeed is that tolerable (ἀνεκτός) of you saying that, if those now reigning (βασιλεύω) over us, persuaded (πείθω) by you, be captured (ἁλίσκομαι), you will persuade those reigning next, then others, if those too be captured, and others upon others, until, all those persuaded by you being captured, some one rule/government (ἀρχή), having become sober-minded (σωφρονέω) and having foreseen (προοράω) what is happening, will destroy (διόλλυμι) you all with your whole race (παγγενεί), before itself perishing first (προαπόλλυμαι).' [Origen] To speak about these things reason does not demand (οὐχ αἱρεῖ λόγος); for none of us says concerning those now reigning that, if persuaded they be captured, we will again persuade those after them, and those being captured we will again persuade the next. And from where did he throw out (ἀπορρίπτω) that, by succession (διαδοχή) the later ones always being persuaded by us and captured through not warding off (ἀμύνομαι) the enemies, some one rule, having become sober and foreseeing what happens, will destroy us with the whole race? But he seems, joining nonsense (φλυαρία) in succession in these things, to have shrieked/blurted out (ἀπορροιβδέω) this too from himself.
pass_b_english: Then again, as is his habit, Celsus muddles things together in what follows, saying what none of us has ever written. For he says something like this: “Nor is it tolerable when you say that, if those who now reign over us are persuaded by you and are taken captive, you will persuade those who reign after them, then others, if they too are taken, and others after others, until, when all who are persuaded by you are being taken, some one government, coming to its senses and foreseeing what is happening, will wipe you all out, race and all, before it is itself destroyed.”

There is no call to speak about this, for none of us says about those who now reign that, if they are persuaded and are taken, we will in turn persuade those after them, and when those are taken we will again persuade the next. And where did he get the idea he has thrown out here, that, as later rulers are always persuaded by us in succession and are taken because they do not defend themselves against the enemy, some one government, coming to its senses and foreseeing what is happening, will wipe us out, race and all? It seems rather that here, stringing one piece of nonsense onto another, he has also blurted this out from his own head.

choices.choice: Celsus’s words are in double quotation marks; Origen’s restatement is his own reply. ἁλῶσι is rendered ‘taken captive’ / ‘taken’ (conquered by enemies), as Origen’s paraphrase ‘because they do not defend themselves against the enemy’ shows. οἱ νῦν βασιλεύοντες ἡμῶν: Celsus speaks as a subject of Rome (‘reign over us’). παγγενεί rendered ‘race and all’ (utter destruction of the whole people). οὐχ αἱρεῖ λόγος taken in its idiomatic sense ‘reason does not require’, hence ‘there is no call’. ἀπερροιβδηκέναι (literally ‘to have shrieked out’) rendered ‘blurted out from his own head’ for ἀφ᾿ ἑαυτοῦ. No Scripture quoted or alluded to.
πρὶν αὐτὴν προαπολέσθαι: dropped the doubled 'before ... first' to 'before it is itself destroyed'

anf_compare.notes: Crombie (ANF 1872) and Chadwick (1953) were not used or consulted; the English is from the Greek.
